This often leads to suboptimal decisions on how to leverage the respective peer, or even misleads into thinking a peer is useless while it is not. 🤔 I've experimented a bit with simply re-sending `STATUS` after some time to a peer, but this seems not to be answered, also the specs https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/master/caps/eth.md#status-0x00 state: > This message should be sent just after the connection is established and prior to any other eth protocol messages. Anyone from <@&652918665943056397> geth or another client here who can give some insight how you deal with this situation? excerpts.author: holgerd77
excerpts.content:
Hi there, Holger from EthereumJS. We are currently battling a bit with outdated `STATUS` information (so things like best hash, fork ID) for peers in our client when peers are already in the peer pool for some  time and the initial **devp2p `ETH` protocol `STATUS`** exchange happened some longer time ago.

This often leads to suboptimal decisions on how to leverage the respective peer, or even misleads into thinking a peer is useless while it is not. 🤔

I've experimented a bit with simply re-sending `STATUS` after some time to a peer, but this seems not to be answered, also the specs https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/blob/master/caps/eth.md#status-0x00 state:

> This message should be sent just after the connection is established and prior to any other eth protocol messages.

Anyone from <@&652918665943056397> geth or another client here who can give some insight how you deal with this situation? Also pinging <@360491619402776577> since he has worked on the latest ETH protocol iterations.

Is this (re-sending `STATUS` messages) worth to loosen in the protocol? Or is this "in fact" already loosened?
